jokes.punchline: Duncan's perfectly timed pivot — from witnessing Jeff's emotional exposure to immediately asking for a cab and payment — is an expert comedic sidestep
jokes.explanation: Duncan's refusal to acknowledge Jeff's emotional moment in favor of a practical request is perfectly timed comic relief. 'Pay for it' as an addendum is a good kicker — he's not just asking for a ride, he wants Jeff to foot the bill while still wounded. Good character economy.

jokes.text: Must have been some kind of trouble. Ah... What a relief that would be.
jokes.setup: Duncan rationalizes why the group didn't call; Jeff's response is sincere-but-ironic
jokes.punchline: 'What a relief that would be' — Jeff's response to the idea that the group had trouble is a reflexive dismissal that immediately sounds hollow given what we've just seen
jokes.explanation: Jeff's reflexive 'what a relief' rings false in the context of the voicemail moment — the comedy is in the disconnect between what he says and what his face (and the audience) knows. Good character beat but relatively minor.

jokes.text: Tell you what, if you need me, I'm gonna be waiting for my cab down here. Having a special nap.
jokes.setup: Duncan prepares to leave Jeff's apartment
jokes.punchline: 'Having a special nap' as a description of passing out drunk while waiting for a cab — a cheerfully euphemistic framing of his impaired state
jokes.explanation: 'Having a special nap' is a great Duncan euphemism. The word 'special' does the comedic work — it's the kind of gentle self-delusion that characterizes Duncan's relationship with his drinking. 'False alarm on that one' and 'special nap' as paired beats in this episode build a quietly funny picture of Duncan's functional alcoholism.

jokes.text: Thanks, bro. I'll be gone in the morning. Yeah. Whatever. Okay. Maybe I stay a while. Thirsty. Don't push it.
jokes.setup: Jeff grudgingly allows Chang to stay; Chang immediately tests the limits
jokes.punchline: 'Okay. Maybe I stay a while' — Chang immediately renegotiating 'I'll be gone in the morning' — followed by 'Thirsty' as an instant demand on his new host
jokes.explanation: Chang's 'maybe I stay a while' is an immediate backslide from his reassurance, and 'Thirsty' is a brilliantly simple first demand. 'Don't push it' is the perfect straight-man response. This beat confirms the Chang storyline's comedic logic: he will always immediately overreach. The escalation from 'gone in the morning' to 'thirsty' in three lines is very efficient.

jokes.text: It might not shock you guys to hear the real reason we had a fight today... It wasn't about the Barenaked Ladies. Although I do have some unresolved issues there.
jokes.setup: Jeff addresses the study group at the dance, explaining the BNL fight
jokes.punchline: 'Although I do have some unresolved issues there' — Jeff's aside admitting he actually does have feelings about the Barenaked Ladies, even after framing the fight as being about something else
jokes.explanation: Perfect coda to the BNL running gag. Jeff denies the fight was about BNL (which it wasn't) but then immediately admits he has 'unresolved issues' with the band — which means he cares more than he lets on. The aside undercuts his own speech in the best way. Good payoff to the running gag.

jokes.text: Caring about a person can be scary. Caring about six people can be a horrifying, embarrassing nightmare.
jokes.setup: Jeff addresses his emotional growth and what the group means to him
jokes.punchline: The escalation from 'scary' (caring about one person) to 'horrifying, embarrassing nightmare' (caring about six) — Jeff's emotional honesty expressed through the language of disaster
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines in the episode. The structure is clean — caring for one person is scary, so caring for six is sixfold worse — but the specific word choices ('horrifying, embarrassing nightmare') are perfectly Jeff. He's giving a sincere Valentine's Day speech but can only express love through self-deprecating catastrophizing. The joke is emotionally honest AND funny, which is Community at its best. Highly quotable.

jokes.text: Be mine? Right! Yes! Love you. Amazing! You're cute? No, wait. Kiss me. There has got to be a way to make money off of this!
jokes.setup: Jeff's speech moves the group to affectionate chaos; everyone responds at once
jokes.punchline: The group's simultaneous overlapping Valentine's reactions — including someone (Troy presumably) saying 'There has got to be a way to make money off of this!' in response to 'You're cute?' — is a perfect tonal collision of genuine sentiment and opportunism
jokes.explanation: The chaos beat is funny in its ensemble energy. 'There has got to be a way to make money off of this!' as a response to romantic sentiment is a good character note — someone is always monetizing in this group. The overlapping dialogue implies warmth plus the group's characteristic absurdity.

jokes.text: Be mine? / Right! Yes!
jokes.setup: Jeff's speech includes reaching out to Pierce; Pierce responds
jokes.punchline: Pierce responding 'Right! Yes!' to being cared for — with his own 'Be mine?' callback — is a sweet and funny button on the Pierce/Valentine subplot
jokes.explanation: A warm callback that closes the Pierce subplot. 'Right! Yes!' as Pierce's acceptance of belonging has genuine feeling, and the callback to the Valentine's candy joke gives the emotional beat a comedic texture.

jokes.text: I've been cheating. No. It says email me.
jokes.setup: Someone appears to confess to cheating (a loaded Valentine's Day admission)
jokes.punchline: The 'cheating' refers to something on a card — 'it says email me' — a Valentine's card message, completely deflating the dramatic reading
jokes.explanation: Brief misdirection gag at the episode's close. The setup (cheating confession) and deflation (Valentine's card) works as a quick tag but lacks character specificity — it's unclear who is saying this and to whom, which weakens it. Mid-to-low tier — functional but minor.

tmdb_overview: On Valentine's Day, Troy and Abed compete for the attention of an assistant librarian, while Britta tries to show she's open-minded about lesbians.
insight: Escalation-driven character comedy sustains 61 jokes across a romantic-misfire episode.
